narrator.rule: The narrator only says what the profile says. Every sentence can be traced to a section, a claim or the music/movement DNA.
narrator.identity: one narrator for the whole atlas: the same face and animation everywhere; a native-speaker voice of the same character per language (studio-grade); the viewer chooses the language

scenes.title: Cold open
narration: The Apache: Paris's Most Dangerous Dance.
This is Apache. Early 20th century.
on_screen: Hero video, first 10 seconds (3TAxfqPbl8U)
Title card: Apache · France · Early 20th century

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The dance originated in 1908 Paris, created by performers Maurice Mouvet and Max Dearly after observing street gangs.
It was popularized at the Moulin Rouge and through early silent films.
The name was adopted from the press's label for local street gangs, which in turn was borrowed from North American Indigenous tribes.
on_screen: Map: France · Europe
Image 1 with attribution

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Originally a theatrical performance piece for cabarets and music halls.
It serves as a dramatic representation of urban conflict and the volatile dynamics of a street-level relationship.
Today it is a revived tradition.
on_screen: Footage: File:How to make a MOTIONER - 01.webm (https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/0/08/How_to_make_a_MOTIONER_-_01.webm?utm_source=commons.wikimedia.org&utm_campaign=imageinfo&utm_content=original)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance is performed as a couple.
It alternates between a rhythmic waltz and violent, acrobatic sequences.
The man leads the woman through throws, lifts, and mock strikes.
Watch for The Throw, The Lift.
on_screen: Hero video full screen, 30–45 s (3TAxfqPbl8U)
Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: Couple-based, utilizing stage space for dramatic movement
scenes.music: diegetic (the video's own sound), underscore under narration

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The music is typically a waltz, most famously 'Valse des Rayons' by Jacques Offenbach.
Other arrangements include 'Valse Chaloupée' by Charles Dubourg and 'Valse Apache' by Fernand Le Borne.
Listen for the Orchestra, Piano.
The pulse is 3/4.
A dramatic, orchestral waltz that transitions between melodic, flowing sections and sharp, rhythmic accents to underscore the physical combat.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Max Dearly, Maurice Mouvet, Mistinguett, Leona, and later performers like Clara Bow and Buster Keaton.
Known as 'Valse Chaloupée' or 'Tough Dance' in various contexts.
Evolved from Parisian street culture and the 'cake-walk' variations performed by Mistinguett.

music_brief.prompt: Original instrumental composition in the musical world of Apache (France). Meter 3/4. Instruments: Orchestra, Piano. Mood: Dramatic, Violent, Sensual, Tense. It should sound like this: A dramatic, orchestral waltz that transitions between melodic, flowing sections and sharp, rhythmic accents to underscore the physical combat.
